# Maskin

> The open-source, MCP-native system where your whole team — humans and AI agents — closes the loop together, from customer signal to shipped bet to measured outcome, with shared memory and a real process. Think of it as the default system for setting up agentic teams: connect Claude (or any MCP client) and drive the workspace directly.

Maskin gives humans and AI agents one shared place to work. Everything flows through a single pipeline — **Insights → Bets → Tasks** — that people and agents read and write together, so context compounds instead of getting lost in scattered chat histories. Maskin is MCP-native and API-first: the UI, agents, and your Claude client all drive the same HTTP surface, and the MCP tools are a thin layer over it.

Run it two ways: **self-hosted** (one `docker-compose` file, free under Apache 2.0) or **managed**. Agent sessions run Claude Code or Codex: self-hosted and Enterprise workspaces use your own Anthropic or OpenAI access, while trial, Pro and Team use a Maskin-funded route.

Setup in one line — connect Claude to a Maskin instance over MCP, then ask Claude to call `get_started`:
`claude mcp add --transport http maskin https://<your-maskin-host>/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer <MASKIN_API_KEY>" --header "X-Workspace-Id: <WORKSPACE_ID>"`

## Top pages

- [Maskin homepage](https://maskin.io/): The product pitch — what Maskin is, how the closed loop from insight to shipped bet works, and the two ways to run it (self-hosted, managed).
- [Free onboarding, then Managed Service](https://maskin.io/onboarding/): A free 60 minute onboarding where the Maskin Team sets up a company's workspace and first self-learning loop live, on its own stack, followed by an optional monthly Managed Service for business consulting and workflow and automation set-up. Every loop learns from what it just shipped and graduates from dry run to semi-autonomous or fully autonomous, with humans keeping the calls that matter. Includes the loop shapes teams start with, how it runs, and what "graduated" means.
- [Maskin for small and growing businesses](https://maskin.io/small-business/): For teams of 5 to 50. Hire AI agents that draft quotes, chase late invoices, answer customer enquiries and send a Monday summary, in the tools the team already uses. The Maskin Team does the setup, every job starts in draft-only mode, and a person approves each result before anything goes out. Includes how it works (hire, brief, approve), a worked example of one job and answers to common questions.
- [Maskin intro deck](https://maskin.io/deck/): The web-native intro deck — five sections in one scroll (cover, vision, the loop, use cases, get started). The lead leave-behind sent after a first meeting; primary CTA is a meeting booking at maskin.io/bookseb.
- [MCP server](https://maskin.io/mcp-server): The Maskin MCP server — the tool surface Claude and other MCP-native agents use to drive a Maskin workspace over HTTP or stdio.
- [Marketplace](https://maskin.io/marketplace/): Outcome-first loops you can run on Maskin — the SEO publishing loop, the outbound loop, the LLM knowledge wiki loop. Each closes the loop on an outcome (page ranked, reply landed, citation resolved), with humans on the gate and agents on the mechanics.
- [Alternatives](https://maskin.io/alternatives/open-source-jira-alternative/): Head-to-head comparisons with existing tools — currently the open-source Jira alternative, more comparison pages landing on the same path.

## Marketplace

- [The SEO publishing loop](https://maskin.io/marketplace/seo-publishing/): One shaped SEO bet in, one indexed, snippet-eligible article on your site out. Research → draft → human approval → publish (HTML + JSON-LD + canonical + per-page og-image + sitemap and llms.txt registration) → weekly rank tracking. Loop closes on a ranked page, not on a written draft. Composed from the SEO content loop plus the Ubersuggest + GitHub MCPs.
- [The outbound loop](https://maskin.io/marketplace/outbound/): Cold prospects in, approved outreach and reply-routed conversations out. Human-on-the-loop with an approval gate on every send; override rate tracked as the honest oversight metric. Sender lane via Unipile (LinkedIn) or Postmark / Resend (email); replies routed back into the workspace as fresh signals. Loop closes on a routed reply that advances, not on a message sent.
- [The lead qualification loop](https://maskin.io/marketplace/lead-qualification/): Inbound leads read the moment they land and gated by a human before a rep works them. Three agent reads (account fit against your ICP, buyer role, intent signal) feed a human promote-or-reject call; every rejection stamps a typed reason on the record, and the qualifier clusters those reasons weekly into an ICP update a human approves. Framework-agnostic (BANT, MEDDIC and others fit inside the loop as typed fields); the qualifier agent runs on your own model keys and is inspectable end to end. Includes a six-question FAQ on lead qualification in sales and marketing, and a comparison with black-box AI lead-scoring tools. Loop closes on a promoted lead a rep works or a rejection with a reason that sharpens the next read, not on a score written to a CRM field.
- [The LLM knowledge wiki loop](https://maskin.io/marketplace/knowledge-wiki/): Team memory that new hires and new agents bootstrap from — indexed, typed, MCP-native. An LLM wiki is a knowledge base an LLM compiles from your own sources into interlinked pages agents read before they answer. A closed bet fires the loop; agents write the verdict and index the artifact; a human gates the taste-sensitive summaries. Loop closes on a page a new hire or a new agent can read to answer a question without asking a person.
- [The product discovery loop](https://maskin.io/marketplace/product-discovery/): Customer signal to shipped bet, on Maskin's typed object graph. Interviews, tickets, and reviews land as typed insight on the same graph as the bets you're already shipping; agents cluster themes and draft candidate bets; a human gates the read-through and the shaping; after ship, the loop re-checks the signal so you know whether the bet actually retired the pain. Loop closes on a shipped bet mapped back to the signal that motivated it, not on an interview scheduled.
- [The LinkedIn content loop](https://maskin.io/marketplace/linkedin-content/): A founder-voice LinkedIn presence run from what actually happened in the business, planned two weeks at a time. Maskin reads the last fortnight of shipped work, feedback and signals, writes interview questions for each account owner, plans a calendar of up to 10 posts and drafts them in one pass in each account’s voice; an editor agent checks every draft and the account owner approves every post before it goes live. Voice is a per-account workspace skill signed off by its owner. Loop closes on a post live on LinkedIn and a retro that has read how it did, not on a draft generated.
- [The product delivery loop](https://maskin.io/marketplace/product-delivery/): Agentic software development with a human on the merge. A shaped bet goes in; Maskin checks its success criteria can be measured, plans the work into owned tasks, has a developer agent build each one and a reviewer agent check it against its task, then runs a release check before a human approves the merge to main. After ship it reads product data and customer feedback and posts a Won, Lost or Inconclusive verdict. Runs per bet alongside Jira or Linear. Loop closes on a verdict and the owner's final call, not on a merged pull request.
- [The competitive intelligence loop](https://maskin.io/marketplace/competitive-intelligence/): Competitor changelogs, pricing pages, GitHub release notes and Product Hunt launches become typed signal, routed into two lanes at once: a battlecard update for sales and, where the signal reveals a real gap, a shaped bet for product with a win condition. Sales enablement approves the battlecard, a PM approves the bet, and both lanes close, instead of the product-facing signal dying in a dashboard. Includes a five-question FAQ on competitor intelligence and a comparison with Klue, Crayon and Contify. Loop closes on a battlecard live in the sales channel and a bet measured against competitor close-rate, not on a dashboard updated.

## Articles

- [What is an agentic workspace?](https://maskin.io/docs/what-is-an-agentic-workspace/): The category Maskin is built around — a shared surface where humans and AI agents work on the same typed objects, and the closed loop (insight → bet → task → shipped → repeat) that defines it.
- [What is MCP-native?](https://maskin.io/docs/what-is-mcp-native/): The Model Context Protocol and why Maskin is built around it — MCP-native means the protocol is the substrate, not an afterthought, and makes bring-your-own-model real. Part of the agentic-workspace cluster (what-is-an-agentic-workspace, ai-product-management-tool, bet-based-product-planning).
- [MCP-native workspace: a category, not a checkbox](https://maskin.io/docs/mcp-native-workspace/): The category above individual MCP servers — a shared, typed object graph where the entire product surface is exposed to agents through MCP. Four architectural markers separate it from an app-with-an-MCP-integration, plus the marketplace-vs-category and AI21-sandbox-workspace disambiguations. Companion to the what-is-mcp-native cornerstone.
- [What is a stateful orchestration substrate?](https://maskin.io/docs/what-is-a-stateful-orchestration-substrate/): The shared, typed store that carries state between stateless AI agents so a pipeline produces coherent work across handoffs. Names handoff amnesia as an architectural failure mode (LongRCA Bench: top diagnostic tools score 13.2% root-step accuracy on long-horizon runs), catalogues five independent August-2026 sources converging on the same fix pattern (RedHat, Recuris, Empirical, ZS Associates, DEV Community), and frames Maskin's typed-object graph as one shape of the substrate. Part of the agentic-workspace cluster.
- [Agent observability: when the workspace is the trace](https://maskin.io/docs/agent-observability/): Agent observability is the discipline of tracing, evaluating, and monitoring what an AI agent does across a multi-step task — a tier above LLM observability where the trace unit is a task with tool calls and decisions rather than a single model call. The load-bearing frame the definitional SERP does not name: a typed workspace graph IS the agent-level trace, so the audit trail is a side effect of the work rather than a separate telemetry pipeline. Covers the LLM-obs-vs-agent-obs vocabulary bridge, the three-layer stack (model tier / loop tier / substrate tier), continuous eval-as-a-loop as the wedge past Anthropic's pre-deploy framing, and the current OSS tools (Langfuse, Arize Phoenix, LangSmith, OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions). Part of the agentic-workspace cluster.
- [What is loop engineering in AI?](https://maskin.io/docs/what-is-loop-engineering/): Loop engineering is designing the system that prompts an AI agent (triggers, checks, stopping conditions and human gates) instead of writing one better prompt. Covers where the term came from (Marily Nika, Addy Osmani, mid-2026), how it differs from prompt, harness and graph engineering, the horizontal primitives every loop-engineered system uses, silence and stopping conditions as the design frontier, where the frame is oversold, and loops as first-class workspace objects in Maskin. Part of the agentic-workspace cluster.
- [Ambient agent workspace: the workspace-graph is the fifth post-chat pattern](https://maskin.io/docs/ambient-agent-workspace/): Chat breaks around 30 seconds and background/ambient AI needs push, not pull. Names workspace-graph-as-inbox as the fifth pattern alongside Adaline's four (verb surface, generative canvas, delegated agent, ambient capture) and LangChain's Agent Inbox, with the four failure modes ambient agents share and how a typed object graph carries state across many parallel loops. Part of the agentic-workspace cluster.
- [What is an Agent Inbox? (LangChain's ambient-agent UX pattern)](https://maskin.io/docs/agent-inbox/): Harrison Chase's definitional post at LangChain (Jan 2025) named the Agent Inbox as the UX for ambient agents — a queue where the agent posts three interrupt types to a human (notify, question, review) instead of running a chat. Definitional citations, the LangGraph open-source reference UI, the Superhuman shipped example, and when the flat queue starts to buckle in favor of the workspace-graph. Tail companion to the ambient-agent-workspace cornerstone.
- [Composable AI agents vs AI employees: the two camps of the agent workspace market](https://maskin.io/docs/composable-ai-agents-vs-ai-employees/): The agent workspace market split in 2026 between AI employees (personas with titles and budgets on a synthetic org chart) and composable AI agents (small agents firing on typed objects, with bounded human gates). Names the load-bearing cut (protocol vs sandbox), the three properties composable treats as first-class (determinism, safety, scale), the honest strengths and costs of each camp, a one-table comparison, and a three-question heuristic for choosing. Sibling to the ambient-agent-workspace piece: that one is the UX split, this one is the architecture split.
- [What are agent skills? Anthropic's SKILL.md primitive, with a Maskin workspace example](https://maskin.io/docs/learn/agent-skills/): An agent skill is a folder with a SKILL.md file that teaches an AI agent one job — a short name and description up top, plus any scripts or reference docs the job needs. Explains the folder layout and frontmatter, progressive disclosure in three levels (metadata always loaded, SKILL.md body on relevance, bundled files on demand), how skills differ from tools, prompts, cursor rules, and workflows, where to find agent skills and what an "agent skills marketplace" means, whether SKILL.md is an open standard (agentskills.io), and how a skill fires on workspace state in a Maskin loop rather than on a chat message. Pairs with the agent-skills-vs-MCP-vs-cursor-rules-vs-workflows comparison and the closed-loop-workspace / stateful-orchestration-substrate pieces.
- [Human in the loop: the approval gate before side-effecting tool calls](https://maskin.io/docs/learn/human-in-the-loop/): Four major agent-SDK vendors — OpenAI (`needs_approval`, `RunState`), Cloudflare (`waitForApproval()`, MCP elicitation), Microsoft (`RequestPort`), Temporal (signal-based approval) — shipped the same primitive in 2025-2026: a named contract that pauses an agent before it invokes a tool that would act on the world. Explains the primitive, the four API surfaces that name it, why the contract is necessary and not sufficient, the four dominant approval surfaces (inbox, chat, MCP elicitation, workspace-graph), and what a typed workspace adds on top — a decision recorded next to the work it approves, not just a paused run. The SDK-contract companion to the human-in-the-loop-AI vocabulary piece.
- [Human on the loop: the honest oversight pattern for autonomous agents](https://maskin.io/docs/learn/human-in-the-loop-ai/): Human on the loop (HOTL) means a person supervises an autonomous agent through review surfaces and named escalation gates instead of approving every action; human in the loop (HITL) means nothing commits until a person approves. Compares the two with a table, uses override rate (0% is rubber-stamping, above 20% is a broken model) and override latency as the honest test, explains that EU AI Act Article 14 does not mandate HITL by name (Article 14(4)(a) to (e) lists five duties: understand and monitor, resist automation bias, interpret the output, decide to override, intervene or stop), and argues for a tiered approval policy enforced at the governance layer, not inside agent code. Pairs with the human-in-the-loop SDK-primitive companion and the ambient-agent-workspace piece.
- [The three tiers of AI-native work — the closure diagnostic](https://maskin.io/docs/three-tiers-ai-native-work/): The tier-comparison hub above the trilogy. Sorts the AI-native tool landscape by object of work and the event that closes the loop — coding agents on a merged PR, task trackers with AI summaries on a status change, knowledge spaces on a page view — and names the closure diagnostic that separates artifact-closing tools from outcome-closing tools. Frames the agentic workspace as a fourth tier where the object of work is a shaped bet with a win condition and the terminal event is a validated outcome. Interlinks to all three tier spokes (ai-product-workspace-vs-coding-agent, ai-product-management-tool, agentic-workspace-vs-knowledge-space) and the cornerstone; preempts the false-closure vocabulary collision with agent-lifecycle-framework research.
- [AI product management tool: the loop, not a tracker](https://maskin.io/docs/ai-product-management-tool/): Why an AI product management tool should close the loop between learning and shipping — insight becomes a testable bet, owned jointly by humans and agents — instead of bolting summaries onto a task tracker.
- [AI product workspace vs AI coding agent](https://maskin.io/docs/ai-product-workspace-vs-coding-agent/): Two agentic tiers, not competitors. A coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, plus the eleven open-source control planes shipped Feb–Aug 2026) terminates on a merged PR; an AI product workspace terminates on a validated outcome against a shaped bet's win condition. Self-hosting, MCP, and approval queues are now table stakes on both tiers — the honest differentiator is the object model beneath the dashboard. Most teams that ship software will run both. The third leg of the tier-comparison cluster alongside the tracker-tier (ai-product-management-tool) and notes-tier (agentic-workspace-vs-knowledge-space) companions.
- [Claude Code vs Codex: pick by job, keep one record](https://maskin.io/docs/claude-code-vs-codex/): Claude Code and Codex compared from each vendor's own docs (accounts, instruction files, MCP, subagents, license), a three-PR bake-off to run on your own repo, what breaks when a team uses both, and the four-field record that keeps decisions outside either tool.
- [Claude Code vs Cursor: pick by job, keep one record](https://maskin.io/docs/claude-code-vs-cursor/): Claude Code (terminal first) and Cursor (editor first) compared from each vendor's own docs: accounts and models, instruction files, hooks and guardrails, non-interactive and cloud runs, a five-check way to choose by job, what breaks when a team uses both, and the four-field record that keeps decisions outside either tool.
- [Claude Code vs GitHub Copilot: pick by job, keep one record](https://maskin.io/docs/claude-code-vs-github-copilot/): Claude Code (terminal first) and GitHub Copilot (editor and GitHub first) compared from each vendor's own docs: plans and sign-in, instruction files, the Copilot CLI and cloud agent, Claude as a third-party agent on a Copilot subscription, a five-check way to choose by job, what breaks when a team uses both, and the four-field record that keeps decisions outside either tool.
- [Claude Cowork vs Claude Code: what each is for, and when neither fits a team](https://maskin.io/docs/claude-cowork-vs-claude-code/): From Anthropic's own pages: Cowork merged into chat on 16 Sep 2026 while Claude Code stayed separate, a table of what each is for, a choose-by-job list, what does not carry between them (~/.claude setups, skills, plugins), plan and pricing facts, and what a team still needs that neither provides.
- [Agentic workspace vs knowledge space: why Obsidian, Mem, and Confluence stop before the bet](https://maskin.io/docs/agentic-workspace-vs-knowledge-space/): The tier-3 leg of the three-tiers trilogy — knowledge spaces (Obsidian, Mem, Confluence, Raft) own capture and retrieval; the failure mode is closure, not retrieval. The closure diagnostic that separates a tracker-with-narrator from an agentic workspace generalises cleanly to the notes tier: a note without a win condition cannot close a loop on an outcome. Includes the tier-3 comparison spine and the honest case for running both.
- [The closed-loop workspace: what tier 4 of AI-native work actually is](https://maskin.io/docs/closed-loop-workspace/): The fourth spoke of the trilogy hub — the affirmative case. Object of work is a shaped bet with a win condition; terminal event is a shipped change measured against that condition, not an artifact (merge, status change, page view). Names the SDLC-scoped-vs-knowledge-work-scoped cut between Closedloop.ai (MIT, May 2026, PRD→PR→judge review) and Maskin (Apache 2.0, bet with win condition on any team) so an AI-index answer can cite the diagnostic and the scope side by side. Handles the "false closure" vocabulary collision with jpalioto/agent-lifecycle-framework research and the "agentic workspace" head-term overlap. Part of the agentic-workspace cluster.
- [Agent skills vs MCP vs cursor rules vs workflows: what each layer solves](https://maskin.io/docs/agent-skills-vs-mcp-vs-cursor-rules-vs-workflows/): The `agent skills vs MCP` SERP debate is a category mistake. Four different layers — MCP is what an agent can reach (protocol), skills are what it invokes (packaged capability), Cursor rules / AGENTS.md are how it acts (behavioral directives), workflows are who runs when (orchestration). Includes the four-way comparison table, the concrete refund-a-subscription example that ships all four, and the unclaimed anti-frame: skills that fire against typed workspace state rather than a git repo. Part of the agentic-workspace cluster.
- [CLAUDE.md vs AGENTS.md: one instruction file or two, and what changes at team scale](https://maskin.io/docs/claude-md-vs-agents-md/): Keep shared rules in one AGENTS.md and import it from CLAUDE.md with @AGENTS.md. Includes a per-tool table of what Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot and Gemini CLI read (checked against vendor docs on 8 Oct 2026), how nested files behave, symlink vs import, a 20-minute cleanup, and the team-scale gap: rules live per repo and per tool, so role-level rules need a home above the repo.
- [LLM wiki vs RAG: which one your team actually needs](https://maskin.io/docs/llm-wiki-vs-rag/): "LLM wiki vs RAG" is the wrong frame — RAG is a query-time retrieval mechanism, an LLM wiki is a compiled artifact, and they sit at different layers. Grounded in the May 2026 preregistered study (Cochran, arXiv:2605.18490, 13 questions over 24 papers, two blinded LLM judges): no architecture won on evidence organization, citation support, and cost at once — the wiki connected findings better, RAG held the cost line, and the celebrated "compile once, query cheap" intuition was refuted at ~21× more tokens per query. Includes the six-dimension decision table, the six questions that change the answer, and the upkeep argument for running a wiki as a loop rather than a side project.
- [Bet-based product planning: the anti-backlog doctrine](https://maskin.io/docs/bet-based-product-planning/): Shape Up's anti-backlog doctrine, run as a live loop — plan in shaped bets with a win condition instead of a growing queue of tickets, with the bet a machine-readable object owned jointly by humans and agents.
- [How to run bet-based planning: the four-step loop](https://maskin.io/docs/how-to-run-bet-based-planning/): The four repeatable steps for running bet-based planning — shape a bet from raw insight, give it a win condition, run a fixed-size cycle, and close the loop on validation. The how-to companion to the bet-based-product-planning anchor.
- [How to build an AI SDR agent loop in Maskin (MCP + Unipile, HITL approval on outbound)](https://maskin.io/docs/how-to-build-ai-sdr-loop/): Seven-step build guide for running an AI SDR agent loop on Maskin's typed object graph — signal, research, draft, human approval, send via a sender-lane MCP (Unipile for LinkedIn, Postmark/Resend for email), reply routing, close condition. Human-on-the-loop with override rate as the honest metric. The concrete build companion to the open-source-ai-sdr alternatives map.
- [Bet vs backlog: do you want a queue or a loop?](https://maskin.io/docs/bet-vs-backlog/): The head-to-head — a backlog is a queue of tickets that decays into aspiration, a bet is a time-bounded, falsifiable commitment with a win condition run on a fixed cycle. Maskin makes the bet a machine-readable object the loop can actually run on. Part of the bet-based-planning cluster.
- [Self-hosted AI workspace: run Claude or Codex agents on your own infrastructure](https://maskin.io/docs/self-hosted-ai-workspace/): Maskin is fully self-hostable under Apache 2.0 — run the closed loop on your own infrastructure with your own Claude Code or Codex access, in sandboxed microVM sessions. An open-source alternative to Claude Cowork, Codex, or ChatGPT workspaces. Part of the agentic-workspace cluster (what-is-an-agentic-workspace, ai-product-management-tool, what-is-mcp-native).
- [Open source Jira alternative that actually closes the loop](https://maskin.io/alternatives/open-source-jira-alternative/): Plane, OpenProject, and Taiga are open-source Jira alternatives that keep the ticket-and-backlog model. Maskin is Apache 2.0, MCP-native, and replaces the ticket with a bet — a testable hypothesis owned jointly by humans and agents — so the loop from signal to shipped, validated outcome actually closes. Part of the agentic-workspace cluster.
- [Open source Linear alternative: the closed-loop bet workspace](https://maskin.io/alternatives/open-source-linear-alternative/): Plane, Focalboard and OpenProject are capable self-hosted issue trackers, but they keep Linear's issue-and-project object model. Maskin is an Apache 2.0, MCP-native workspace where the unit of work is a bet that runs from signal to a shipped, validated outcome. Compares the object model, licence and closed-loop behaviour, and says who should keep Linear or an OSS tracker instead.
- [Open source Notion alternative for AI product management](https://maskin.io/alternatives/open-source-notion-alternative/): AppFlowy, AFFiNE, Anytype, Docmost, and Outline are open-source Notion clones that preserve the page-and-database object model — and Notion's own 2026 pivot (Custom Agents Feb 2026, Developer Platform May 2026) still bolts the AI onto pages. Maskin replaces the page with a bet — a testable hypothesis with a win condition, jointly owned by humans and agents — so the AI product management loop actually closes. Apache 2.0, MCP-native, self-hostable. Companion to the Jira alt on the /alternatives/ comparison cluster.
- [Open source AI SDR: the six real repos and the loop shape that works](https://maskin.io/alternatives/open-source-ai-sdr/): The honest map of the six OSS AI SDR repos on GitHub in 2026 (MatthewDailey/open-sdr, OpenOutreach, ZeroGTM, Signal, personizeai/revenue-os, kandksolvefast/ai-sdr-agent), the $50-200/mo vs $2k-5k/mo cost split between OSS and closed SaaS (11x, Artisan, Qualified, SalesForge, AiSDR), and the human-on-the-loop shape that makes outbound work instead of getting your domain blacklisted. Companion to the how-to-build-ai-sdr-loop build guide.
- [Open source Codex alternative — closed-loop knowledge-work workspace](https://maskin.io/alternatives/open-source-alternative-to-codex/): OpenAI Codex's terminal event is a merged PR; Maskin's is an outcome validated against a shaped bet's win condition. Apache 2.0, MCP-native, self-hostable, model-agnostic at the MCP protocol layer, with agent sessions running on Claude Code or the Codex CLI. Written for the OpenAI-side buyer whose loop is "ship a decision," not "close a coding ticket." Codex-shaped coding work still runs; the loop past the merge is the extension. Companion to the Claude Cowork alt (mirrors the same argument for the Anthropic-side buyer).
- [Open source alternative to Claude Cowork](https://maskin.io/alternatives/open-source-alternative-to-claude-cowork/): Three honest open-source answers to Claude Cowork, sorted by job. OpenWork (MIT desktop app, local-first, 50+ model providers) for one person's agent on local files; Multica (assigns issues to coding-agent CLIs; Apache 2.0 text plus extra hosting conditions) for a team board of coding agents; Maskin (Apache 2.0, self-hostable) for teams whose agents work on shared insights, bets, and tasks. Covers where teams outgrow Cowork, a four-way comparison table, self-host vs managed, and Maskin's own limits (not a personal-files agent, memory gap, early traction).
- [Self-hosted AI agent control plane for knowledge work (not coding tasks)](https://maskin.io/alternatives/self-hosted-ai-agent-control-plane/): Twelve open-source self-hosted control planes shipped Feb-Aug 2026 (amux, Crewship, Preloop, Nora, Musematic, Mission Control, Clawix, Vornik, Zoink, herdctl, danrex/fleet, VNX) — all Docker/Podman/K8s, approval-first, most MCP-native, and all built around the same object model: a kanban of coding tasks that closes when a PR merges. Maskin sits in the same category on the four table-stakes commodities (Apache-2.0, self-hostable, MCP-native, approval-first) but diverges on the object model — loop on typed objects (insight → bet → task → validated) rather than a kanban of coding tasks. Includes Van Deth's solopreneur/chat-as-primary counter-frame as the honest challenge at n=1 scale. Category-vocabulary page on the /alternatives/ cluster.
- [Self-hosted AI agents in 2026: the OSS landscape, honestly categorised](https://maskin.io/alternatives/self-hosted-ai-agents/): The 2026 self-hosted-AI-agents SERP mixes four categories into one flat list — this page runs the split. Stateful-agent frameworks (Maskin, Letta, Cheshire Cat AI, Agent Zero, Paperclip), workflow-node builders (n8n, Flowise, Dify, EpicStaff), RAG chat frontends (Open WebUI, LibreChat, AnythingLLM, Bionic GPT), and coding-agent control planes (twelve entrants, cross-linked to the sibling page). Filter by object of work first, then by license shape (permissive/copyleft/source-available/fair-code), then by features. Maskin sits in the stateful-agent category. Companion to the closed-loop-workspace essay for the tier-4 framing and the control-plane page for category 4 in full.
- [The operating system for product teams](https://maskin.io/solutions/product-teams/): The product-team landing page. One workspace where the wiki, customer signals, shaped bets, and delivery handoff live together, walked through as a three-step operating system (Knowledge Wiki, Product Discovery, Shaping Bets), each step naming the tool it replaces. Ships each bet either as an epic in an existing Jira/Linear tracker (Path A) or through Maskin's Product Delivery loop (Path B) — equal-weight, pick per bet not per team. Template for the /solutions/* vertical clones (accounting, gp-clinics, etc.).
- [Open source AI agents in 2026: what to run, under which license, and where the work lives](https://maskin.io/alternatives/open-source-ai-agents/): Open source AI agents sorted into four lanes (frameworks, assistants, visual builders, team workspaces) with licenses checked against each GitHub repo on 5 Oct 2026, including the n8n and Dify commercial restrictions, AutoGen's maintenance mode and Flowise's archived status.
- [Open source AI coding agent — the shortlist, honestly tiered](https://maskin.io/alternatives/open-source-ai-coding-agent/): Six open-source AI coding agents sorted by tier rather than flattened into one list — single-developer runtimes, multi-session control planes, and cross-role product workspaces. All free to install; the paid piece is the model API key you bring. Written for the buyer who has seen every listicle collapse the category. Part of the /alternatives/ comparison cluster.
- [n8n alternative: pick by what your runs have to leave behind](https://maskin.io/alternatives/n8n/): Honest n8n alternatives sorted into four shapes: hosted builders (Zapier, Make), open-source and source-available engines (Activepieces, Windmill, Kestra, Node-RED), no-code AI agent platforms (Lindy, Gumloop, MindStudio), and closed-loop workspaces (Maskin). Cites n8n's own docs on its fair-code license and its default execution pruning (336 hours or 10,000 runs), says when to stay on n8n, and notes that Maskin has fewer integrations and no visual canvas. Part of the /alternatives/ comparison cluster.
- [Paperclip alternative for AI agents: when AI employees stop fitting](https://maskin.io/alternatives/paperclip/): Honest Paperclip alternatives sorted into five shapes: code-first orchestration frameworks (CrewAI, LangGraph, AutoGen), agent runtimes (OpenClaw, Hermes), hosted AI workforce platforms (Relevance AI, Lindy), visual automation with agent nodes (n8n, Dify), and typed-object workspaces (Maskin). Cites Paperclip's own README on what it does (atomic task checkout, budgets with hard stops, activity log, routines), lists six reasons people leave, says when to stay on Paperclip (per-agent budget hard stops, mixed agent fleets, community), and includes a five-item audit test before switching. Part of the /alternatives/ comparison cluster.
- [OpenClaw alternative: when a shared record matters more than a shared agent](https://maskin.io/alternatives/openclaw/): Honest OpenClaw alternatives sorted by what you are missing: Hermes Agent for one agent with memory (imports from OpenClaw), NanoClaw, ZeroClaw, PicoClaw and OpenFang for lighter or more isolated runtimes, hosted assistants, and a team workspace like Maskin when the thing to share is a record of decisions and outcomes. Includes OpenClaw's team gateway and its trust limit, a repo-by-repo table of the Claw family, the memory gap Maskin has versus OpenClaw and Hermes, and a ten-minute test before switching.
- [Productboard alternative: what to use instead depends on the job you are missing](https://maskin.io/alternatives/productboard/): Honest Productboard alternatives sorted by the job you are missing: Canny for feedback intake and voting, Jira Product Discovery for a roadmap next to Jira delivery, Aha and ProductPlan for portfolio and roadmap planning, Linear and Notion as delivery and workspace options, and Maskin when signal, decision and shipped result should be one connected record. Vendor facts read from each vendor's own pages on 26 October 2026 (Productboard publishes no prices; Business and Enterprise plans are priced by makers). Says when to stay on Productboard (customer portal with voting, stakeholder roadmap views, large orgs, 25+ integrations) and that Maskin has no portal, voting or roadmap views. Includes a ten-minute test before switching. Part of the /alternatives/ comparison cluster.
- [Agentic workflow vs closed loop: three patterns, not two](https://maskin.io/docs/learn/agentic-workflow-vs-closed-loop/): An agentic workflow is a predetermined step chain with an LLM slotted in; an agent decides its own next step; the closed loop is a third pattern — a workflow-shaped container with an entry condition, typed objects, human-taste gates, and a close condition, with agent execution inside the shape. The vocabulary bridge for teams conflating all three.
- [AI agent governance for small teams](https://maskin.io/docs/learn/ai-agent-governance/): Agent actions that are attributable, permissioned, and auditable — at small-team scale. Typed permissions on agent identities, first-class driver attribution on every action, and an audit trail that lives on the same object graph as the work, instead of enterprise SSO/SCIM/RBAC/SOC 2 altitude. Answers "who let this agent do that, and can we prove it?"
- [Agent orchestration, agentic loops, and control planes: which one a small team needs](https://maskin.io/docs/learn/agent-orchestration/): Agent orchestration is the coordination layer between multiple AI agents; the agentic loop is the shape of one agent's work; the agent control plane is the governance around both. Reads the three overlapping terms as one stack with three concerns, with a side-by-side table (problem solved, buyer, primitive, failure mode, when it starts to matter) and the order a small team should adopt them: model the loop first, add orchestration when work branches across agents, add a control plane when a second person needs to know what the agents did. Includes seven FAQs (orchestration vs workflow, vs MCP, do I need a framework).
- [Ralph Wiggum loop: how it works, and when "keep trying" needs a verdict](https://maskin.io/docs/learn/ralph-wiggum-loop/): The Ralph Wiggum loop feeds the same prompt to a coding agent over and over until a stop signal fires (Geoffrey Huntley, July 2025; Anthropic's Claude Code ralph-wiggum plugin). Covers how it works step by step, what it is good at, where its own makers say it stops, and what a closed loop adds around it: a close condition written before the work starts, an owner and a recorded verdict.
- [Agent memory across sessions: what has to survive](https://maskin.io/docs/learn/agent-memory-across-sessions/): Only three things are worth carrying from one run to the next — decisions (what was chosen and why), corrections (what a human changed after the fact), and artifacts (what the run produced). If a scheduled agent wakes up Monday with no idea what it decided Friday, one of the three fell on the floor.
- [Claude Code for product managers: what it covers, where it stops](https://maskin.io/docs/learn/claude-code-for-product-managers/): What Claude Code does for PM work (specs, research synthesis, updates, Slack and Linear over MCP), how a non-engineer sets it up (folder, CLAUDE.md, skills), what it remembers between sessions (CLAUDE.md is shared via git, auto memory is machine-local), and the four points where a shared team record takes over: a second person needs the work, a decision needs its reason, a bet needs an outcome check, a signal needs to link to the decision it moved. Read against Anthropic's docs on 8 October 2026.
- [Claude Code agent teams: when they are enough, and when a team needs a shared record](https://maskin.io/docs/learn/claude-code-agent-teams/): Agent teams are an experimental Claude Code feature where one lead session spawns teammates that share a task list and a mailbox inside one session. Enough for one developer, one repo, one sitting; not enough when a second person, a decision with its reason, or an outcome check must outlast the session. Includes lighter options to try first and the four boundaries where a shared record starts to matter.
- [Claude Code team: how to share context and decisions, not six private setups](https://maskin.io/docs/learn/claude-code-team/): A Claude Code team shares setup and context through git (the committed settings file, project skills, one CLAUDE.md with an owner) but not Claude's own notes, which are machine-local. Covers what /team-onboarding does and does not do (a snapshot of one person's last 30 days, no decisions or owners), why a rule file is a request and a hook is a lock, and a small record of owner, decision with reason and check date. Includes a first-week checklist and where the record can live. No plan, seat or price advice. Read against Anthropic's docs on 2026-10-15.
- [Claude Code memory: one person's notes, or a record the whole team shares](https://maskin.io/docs/learn/claude-code-memory/): Claude Code memory is two things: CLAUDE.md files you write and auto memory the notes Claude writes for itself. Both load at the start of every session; only CLAUDE.md can be shared through git, while auto memory is machine-local. Covers where each is stored, what loads (the first 200 lines or 25KB of MEMORY.md), how to turn auto memory off or clear it, the Claude API memory tool, and a four-step way for a team to share what Claude learns plus a shared record for decisions and owners. Companion to Claude Code team.
- [How to choose a knowledge layer for your agents — a decision guide](https://maskin.io/docs/learn/choose-a-knowledge-layer/): Decision-stage walk across the four architectures agent knowledge can live in — retrieval-beside (Mem0), stateful-runtime (Letta), temporal-knowledge-graph (Zep), and typed workspace graph (Maskin). Two structural questions (what survives between runs; who reads it without tooling) collapse the field faster than any vendor horse race, plus the composition patterns that beat picking one architecture and hoping.
- [What is an agent harness? A plain definition, the main options, and where the work lands](https://maskin.io/docs/learn/what-is-an-agent-harness/): An agent harness is everything in an AI agent except the model: the prompts, tools, context handling, permissions and loop that turn a model's answers into actions (LangChain's shorthand: Agent = Model + Harness). Covers the eight parts inside a harness, harness vs framework vs runtime in one table, the three kinds of harness (coding, general-purpose, your own) and how to choose, what harness engineering means (guides and sensors), and what a harness does not keep: who owns the work, what was decided and whether it worked. Seven FAQs, including whether Claude Code and MCP count. Maskin is described as the shared record where a harness's work lands, not as a harness.
- [Agentic SDLC: where agents fit across plan, build, review, verify and release, and who approves each step](https://maskin.io/docs/learn/agentic-sdlc/): Agentic SDLC is the software development lifecycle run so that AI agents do the work inside each stage (plan, build, review, verify) and people make the decisions between stages. Six stages (plan, build, review, verify, release, learn) with a table of what the agent does, what a person approves and the evidence that closes each stage. Only three decisions need a person: which bets are worth shaping, the merge to main, and the final call on the bet. Three rules: write measurable Won and Lost criteria first, name one approver per stage (including nobody), check the result after release. Explained through the Product delivery loop. Five FAQs, including agentic SDLC vs the traditional SDLC and vs vibe coding.
- [Agent skills marketplace: how to evaluate one](https://maskin.io/docs/agent-skills-marketplace/): The phrase names three different things — open collections and directories, vendor-hosted libraries, and skills bundled inside a product. Most are discovery surfaces, not commercial marketplaces. Four questions separate a listing from a place skills actually run, gate their output, and persist results.
- [Knowledge wiki vs vector database: artifact vs storage engine](https://maskin.io/docs/knowledge-wiki-vs-vector-database/): A vector database stores embeddings and returns nearest-neighbour matches; a knowledge wiki is a set of compiled, human-auditable pages. Not competitors — the vector database is one component in a retrieval pipeline, the wiki is the artifact you might store in it. You can put wiki pages into a vector database; you cannot retire one with the other. Sibling to the llm-wiki-vs-rag comparison.
- [MCP vs RAG: the wire and the retrieval layer are not rivals](https://maskin.io/docs/mcp-vs-rag/): MCP is a wire an agent reaches tools over; RAG is a query-time retrieval mechanism. They sit at different layers, neither carries state across runs, and they stack three ways (RAG behind MCP, MCP on top of RAG, both under a state layer). The "vs" frame hides the real question — what carries the decision from run to run.
- [MCP tools vs resources vs prompts: which primitive to expose](https://maskin.io/docs/mcp-tools-vs-resources/): The MCP spec splits the three primitives by who is in control: tools are model-controlled, resources application-driven, prompts user-controlled. A four-question rule for which one to expose, how Claude Code, VS Code and Cursor surface each, and what Maskin's server registers (dozens of tools, three resource templates, no prompts).
- [MCP vs API: when a plain API is enough, and what agents need beyond it](https://maskin.io/docs/mcp-vs-api/): An API is a contract your code calls; MCP is a standard way for an AI agent to discover and call tools at runtime, usually on top of an existing API. A plain API is enough when your code decides the calls; MCP pays off when several agents or clients share tools and the model chooses. For an agent that writes to a team's record, the server matters more than the protocol: typed objects, permissions, an audit trail and an owner on every piece of work. Includes a four-question decision rule, the MCP vs API vs CLI question, and what Maskin's own audit found still missing.
- [At-risk account alerts: when churn signals become bets](https://maskin.io/docs/at-risk-account-alerts/): The churn & expansion loop. Falling usage plus rising errors becomes a shaped recovery bet, and the at-risk alert arrives with full context and a prepared plan instead of a bare dashboard notification. Answers which signals to watch, how this differs from a churn dashboard, where the human stays in the loop, and whether the same loop handles expansion.
- [AI customer feedback loop: from "someone said something" to "we shipped it and told them"](https://maskin.io/loops/ai-customer-feedback-loop/): The customer feedback loop closes the circle from a customer's pain to a shipped fix they are told about: feedback becomes a shaped bet, the bet ships, and the customer is notified. Runs on typed objects (feedback, bet, task) with a human gate on which feedback deserves a bet and whether the outcome counts as a win. Explains why closure, not capture, separates a loop from a feedback inbox or ticketing tool, the three places feedback loops fail, and a five-question FAQ. One of Maskin's five marketplace loops.
- [Competitive intelligence loop: two lanes, one signal, both close](https://maskin.io/loops/competitive-intelligence/): A competitive intelligence loop watches competitor changelogs, pricing pages, GitHub releases and Product Hunt launches and routes every signal into two lanes at once: a draft battlecard update for sales and a shaped bet for product where the signal reveals a real gap. Sales enablement approves the battlecard, a PM approves the bet, and both lanes close. Covers the four moments of the loop, why two-lane routing beats a one-lane CI dashboard, the typed-object model behind it and its honest limits.
- [AI-automatisering: de første opgaver at automatisere (dansk guide)](https://maskin.io/da/ai-automatisering/): Danish-language guide to the first five tasks a small business should hand to an AI agent (lead follow-up, customer inbox, weekly reports, meeting notes to tasks, open-task nudges), four tests for choosing, and a worked lead follow-up example where a human approves before anything is sent. Human in the loop by status change, not by trust.
- [Hvad er en AI agent? Forklaret til dig, der skal beslutte, om virksomheden har brug for en (dansk)](https://maskin.io/da/hvad-er-en-ai-agent/): Danish-language explainer of what an AI agent is, how it differs from a chatbot, an AI assistant and plain automation, three example tasks, what an agent costs to run (model use, setup, oversight, platform), what can go wrong, and a five-question readiness check.
- [AI-agenter: guide for danske virksomheder (dansk)](https://maskin.io/da/ai-agenter/): Danish-language guide to which tasks a company with 11 to 200 employees can give an AI agent (lead follow-up, weekly reports, inbox, meeting notes, customer replies), what agents cannot do, a three-tier approval model, a cost breakdown with a worked example, and the data questions to ask a vendor.
- [Bedste AI-værktøjer til virksomheder: 4 slags og hvordan I vælger (dansk)](https://maskin.io/da/ai-vaerktoejer/): Danish-language overview of the four kinds of AI tool for a business (general assistant, automation engine, single-task tool, shared workspace for agents), five questions for choosing, what to ask a vendor about data, and where Maskin fits and does not fit.
- [AI-agenter: guide för svenska företag (svenska)](https://maskin.io/sv/ai-agenter/): Swedish-language guide to which jobs a company with 11 to 200 employees can give an AI agent (follow-up on enquiries, weekly reports, inbox, meeting minutes, customer replies), what agents cannot do, a three-tier approval model, a cost breakdown with a worked example using invented numbers, and the data questions to ask a vendor.

## Start here

- [Documentation home](https://maskin.io/docs/): Entry point to all Maskin docs.
- [Get started](https://maskin.io/docs/get-started/): What Maskin is, the unified pipeline, and the two ways to run it.
- [Quickstart tutorial](https://maskin.io/docs/quickstart/): Empty instance to an agent doing real work in ~10 minutes, driven from Claude.
- [Self-hosted setup](https://maskin.io/docs/get-started/self-hosted/): Run your own instance with docker-compose and connect Claude over MCP.

## Concepts

- [Core concepts](https://maskin.io/docs/concepts/): Actors (humans and agents), workspaces, the Insights → Bets → Tasks object graph, relationships, comments, triggers, sessions, notifications, skills, files, extensions.
- [Agents & sessions](https://maskin.io/docs/agents/): How agents run — the session lifecycle, logs, token usage, and cost.
- [Architecture](https://maskin.io/docs/architecture/): How the system fits together (server, Postgres, storage, real-time).

## Reference

- [MCP tools](https://maskin.io/docs/mcp-tools/): The full MCP tool surface agents and Claude use to drive a workspace — objects, schema, actors, comments, files, skills, triggers, sessions, notifications, integrations, and LLM keys.
- [API reference](https://maskin.io/docs/api/): The API-first HTTP surface under `/api`, authentication, resource groups, and real-time SSE.
- [OpenAPI spec](https://maskin.io/docs/api/): Each Maskin instance serves a live, authoritative machine-readable API spec at `/openapi.json` (relative to your own instance host, not maskin.io) — point any OpenAPI client or code generator at it.
- [Configuration](https://maskin.io/docs/configuration/): Environment variables and workspace settings.
- [Integrations](https://maskin.io/docs/integrations/): The 12 first-party providers: tools for GitHub, Slack, PostHog and Resend are available to every agent once connected; Linear, Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Meet, Ubersuggest, LinkedIn and Google Search Console (read-only: inspect_url, list_sites) are added per agent; Skjald is provider-only.

- [LLM & models](https://maskin.io/docs/llm/): Supported providers and how model keys work.
- [Production deployment](https://maskin.io/docs/deployment/): Running Maskin beyond localhost.

- [Troubleshooting](https://maskin.io/docs/troubleshooting/): Common setup and connection issues.
